summary: Ten findings the owner reported on the Teach entry page (/teach) on 2026-09-04: hierarchy, affordance, chrome noise, hidden limits, engineer-speak status, misplaced links, copy density, language toggle placement, card affordance, and trust visibility.

items.title: Primary action is unclear (weak visual hierarchy)
items.problem: 'Start a conversation' and 'Upload a dataset file' are given almost equal weight, so a first-time user cannot tell what to try first.
items.fix: Make one path the primary action with a clearly secondary alternative (size, colour, position), based on which door serves a newcomer best; the other remains one click away.

items.title: The 1–5 process steps look like an interactive stepper but are placed under the action buttons
items.problem: '1 Dataset 2 Check 3 Settings 4 Training 5 Result' reads as a clickable progress indicator, yet it sits below the buttons and it is unclear whether it is clickable or informational.
items.fix: Either make it a real stepper (current step highlighted, past steps clickable) placed where progress lives (top of the flow), or restyle it as a plain 'what happens next' explainer with no button-like affordance.

items.title: Global navigation and footer are visual noise for the main task
items.problem: The top nav (Explore knowledge, Live test …) and the footer links (ain-js, aindrive …) pull attention away from the one task on this page: training the model.
items.fix: Reduce chrome on the teach flow pages: a slim header (logo + back/exit + language) and a minimal footer; keep full navigation on marketplace pages.
items.shipped: /teach/* now renders under FocusedLayout — a 56 px header with only the logo, an Exit link to /explore and the language toggle, and a footer reduced to copyright · Terms · Contact — while every marketplace page keeps the full header and footer.

items.title: File limits are hidden in small helper text
items.problem: 'jsonl, csv, tsv … up to 2000 questions' is a hard constraint shown as tiny auxiliary text, so users upload a non-conforming file and hit an error late.
items.fix: Show the accepted formats and the question cap prominently on the upload card (badge/row near the picker) and validate on file selection before upload.

items.title: Node status is engineer-speak
items.problem: 'Teaching on this node: open · 0 waiting …' does not tell an ordinary person whether they can start training right now.
items.fix: Replace with a plain-language readiness line ('You can start now — no queue' / 'N lessons ahead of you, about M minutes') with the technical detail behind a disclosure.

items.title: 'My datasets and lessons →' is placed awkwardly and is easy to miss
items.problem: It sits under the entry buttons, breaking the main action flow, although it is the main route back to existing work.
items.fix: Move it to a consistent secondary position (top-right of the page or the slim header) styled as a navigational link, not as part of the action group.

items.title: Explanatory text is too dense
items.problem: The intro ('Two ways in, one result …') and each card's description are long, preventing quick scanning and causing fatigue.
items.fix: Cut the intro to one line; card descriptions to one short sentence + one benefit; move details behind 'How it works'.

items.title: The language selector sits awkwardly at the top of the main content
items.problem: Placed below the nav at the start of content, it unbalances the layout and does not read as a system setting.
items.fix: Move the language toggle into the header (system-setting area), consistently across pages.

items.title: Card affordance is ambiguous
items.problem: It is unclear whether the whole method card is clickable or only the button inside; hover/feedback states do not resolve it.
items.fix: Make the whole card the click target with a clear hover/focus state, or visually demote the card to a plain container with only the button interactive — not both.

items.title: Trust and safety are not visible at the entry point
items.problem: 'Keep private or publish' exists, but at the moment of choosing a path the user cannot see how uploaded data is protected, who can see it, and what rights they keep.
items.fix: Add a short trust strip on the entry page (private by default · you choose what to publish · your key stays in your browser · what the node operator can see) linking to the full terms.
